shots.narration: Eleven at night, 3 July 1976. Four huge military planes fly over Africa with every light switched off.
shots.onScreen: Four C-130 Hercules in a row, black against a starfield, cloud tops lit by the moon
shots.motion: slow lateral dolly along the formation, camera 30 m below the lead wing

shots.narration: They have come four thousand kilometres from Israel, flying so low that no radar sees them.
shots.onScreen: Parchment map, Israel to Uganda; gold route ribbon grows down the Red Sea; "4,000 KM" counter ticks up
shots.motion: crane down from above Sinai, follow the ribbon south

shots.narration: Near the target, the lead plane shuts down two of its four engines so it lands almost in silence.
shots.onScreen: Close on the wing: two propellers slow and stop, the other two keep turning
shots.motion: push in on the stopping propellers
shots.sfx: engine spool down, propeller whoosh fading

shots.narration: Its ramp opens while it is still rolling. Out comes a black Mercedes, built to look exactly like the car of Uganda's president.
shots.onScreen: Ramp lowers on a dark runway; a black Mercedes and two Land Rovers roll out with flags on the bonnet
shots.motion: low angle from the runway, ramp opens toward camera
shots.sfx: hydraulic whine, ramp clank, car engine

shots.narration: Inside an old airport terminal, a hundred and six hostages are waiting. Their deadline is tomorrow afternoon.
shots.onScreen: Old terminal at night, one window lit, silhouettes of people lying on the floor inside
shots.motion: slow push toward the lit window

shots.narration: The man leading the first team is thirty years old. His name is Yonatan Netanyahu.
shots.onScreen: Yoni in olive uniform and cap, sitting in the Mercedes, eyes calm; name callout

shots.narration: In the next ninety minutes, Israel will try something no army had done before. A rescue in an enemy country, four thousand kilometres from home.
shots.onScreen: The convoy moves toward the terminal, headlights off, the airport tower ahead
shots.motion: camera rises and pulls back to reveal the whole airport

shots.narration: This is Operation Thunderbolt.
shots.onScreen: "OPERATION THUNDERBOLT" slams in over the dark runway, lightning bolt emblem
shots.motion: title slam 1.9x to 1x, then slow push

shots.narration: Let's go back one week. Tel Aviv, Sunday 27 June 1976.
shots.onScreen: Ben Gurion airport, morning sun, an Air France Airbus A300 at the gate
shots.motion: crane down from sky to the jet

shots.narration: Air France Flight 139 is going to Paris, with one stop on the way in Athens.
shots.onScreen: Departure board flips to "AF 139 PARIS VIA ATHENS"

shots.narration: It leaves on time, just before nine in the morning, and turns west over the Mediterranean.
shots.onScreen: Map: Tel Aviv to Athens route ribbon, plane icon travelling

shots.narration: Most of the passengers are Israeli or Jewish. Families, students, pensioners going on holiday.
shots.onScreen: Cabin interior, passengers settling in, a child at the window, an old couple sharing a newspaper

shots.narration: At half past eleven it lands in Athens. Thirty-eight people get off. Fifty-eight get on.
shots.onScreen: Plane at Athens gate, two counters: OFF 38, ON 58

shots.narration: Athens airport in 1976 is not careful. On this day, a metal detector is broken, and nobody is watching the X-ray screen.
shots.onScreen: Security desk: a detector arch with a dead red light, an empty chair in front of the X-ray monitor
shots.motion: push in on the empty chair

shots.narration: Four of the new passengers walk straight through with pistols and grenades in their bags.
shots.onScreen: Four figures carry bags past the empty X-ray desk; bags glow faintly red in an X-ray tint

shots.narration: Two of them sit in first class. Two sit in economy. They look like everyone else.
shots.onScreen: Cutaway cabin, two figures highlighted in first class, two in economy

shots.narration: At ten past twelve, Flight 139 takes off again for Paris.
shots.onScreen: Map: route from Athens heading west

shots.narration: Eight minutes later, over the Gulf of Corinth, the two in first class stand up. Each has a pistol in one hand and a grenade in the other.
shots.onScreen: Silhouettes stand in the first class aisle; weapons shown only as dark shapes, nobody hurt
shots.motion: slow push from the back of the cabin

shots.narration: They run toward the cockpit. The crew and the front rows start screaming. At the back, nobody knows what is happening yet.
shots.onScreen: Split frame: panic at the front, calm at the back with a passenger reading
shots.motion: lateral dolly from front to back

shots.narration: In the cockpit are the captain, Michel Bacos, the co-pilot, and the flight engineer.
shots.onScreen: Cockpit, three crew figures; name callout on the captain
shots.overlay: callout: MICHEL BACOS / CAPTAIN, AIR FRANCE

shots.narration: Bacos hears the screams and sends the engineer out to look.
shots.onScreen: Engineer stands, unlatches the cockpit door

shots.narration: The door opens, and a man is standing right there, with a gun pointed at the engineer's head.
shots.onScreen: Door opens on a silhouette with a raised dark shape; cut before any contact

shots.narration: He is Wilfried Böse, a German. He walks into the cockpit and takes the co-pilot's seat.
shots.onScreen: Böse in the co-pilot seat; name callout in red second line

shots.narration: He tells Bacos to turn the plane south. Do what I say, and nobody gets hurt.
shots.onScreen: Böse points at the compass; heading needle swings from west to south
shots.motion: close on the attitude and heading display

shots.narration: At the back, the other two hijackers take control of economy. In about three minutes, the whole plane is theirs.
shots.onScreen: Two hijackers at the back of economy; a "3:00" stopwatch runs down

shots.narration: Then Böse picks up the captain's microphone. He says the plane is hijacked, and that he is the captain now. He says it again in French.
shots.onScreen: Böse with the cabin microphone; speech waveform icon over the cabin

shots.narration: By the next morning, Flight 139 is on front pages all over the world.
shots.onScreen: Newspapers spin in and stack: "AIR FRANCE JET HIJACKED", "246 HOSTAGES"

shots.narration: Meanwhile, the world asks a question. Who are these four people?
shots.onScreen: Four silhouette cards flip in a row

shots.narration: Two are Palestinian, from a group that split off the Popular Front for the Liberation of Palestine. It is called the PFLP External Operations.
shots.onScreen: Two silhouette cards with the group name

shots.narration: The other two are German. Wilfried Böse and Brigitte Kuhlmann, from a far-left group called the Revolutionary Cells.
shots.onScreen: Böse and Kuhlmann cards, generic house-style figures

shots.narration: Many of their comrades are in prison. Most of them in Israel, others in France, West Germany, Switzerland and Kenya.
shots.onScreen: Map with prison icons; Israel glows brightest
shots.motion: camera drifts across Europe, the Middle East and Africa

shots.narration: The plan is simple and cruel. Take a plane full of hostages and trade them for the prisoners.
shots.onScreen: Plane icon on one side of a scale, prison padlocks on the other

shots.narration: At three in the afternoon the jet reaches Libya. The fuel is running low.
shots.onScreen: Map: plane icon reaching Benghazi; fuel gauge needle near empty
shots.motion: follow plane, push in on Benghazi

shots.narration: Bacos tells the control tower in Benghazi it is land here or crash. Libya lets them land.
shots.onScreen: Cockpit radio exchange, tower silhouette through the window

shots.narration: On the ground, the hijackers relax. They walk off the plane and meet Libyan officials. Passengers are given food.
shots.onScreen: Plane on hot tarmac, hijackers chatting with officials, trays passed into the cabin

shots.narration: One passenger, a young woman, tells them she is pregnant and losing her baby. They let her go. She was not really losing the baby. It was a trick, and it worked.
shots.onScreen: A woman helped down the stairs; a small "her claim at the time" chip
shots.overlay: chip: SHE PRETENDED, SHE WAS RELEASED

shots.narration: After about seven hours and a full tank of fuel, the plane takes off again.
shots.onScreen: Fuel truck pulls away, jet takes off at dusk

shots.narration: Soon after takeoff, Böse tells the captain to fly south. To Uganda.
shots.onScreen: Heading needle swings south again

shots.narration: When the cabin hears the word Uganda, the fear gets worse. Especially for the Israelis.
shots.onScreen: Passengers' faces, worried brows, a hand gripping an armrest

shots.narration: Nobody knows what will happen next. And not knowing is its own kind of fear.
shots.onScreen: Dark cabin, reading lights going off one by one

shots.narration: Meanwhile, Uganda's president is waiting for them. Idi Amin.
shots.onScreen: Statue-like portrait of Amin in uniform with medals, lit from below
shots.overlay: callout: IDI AMIN / PRESIDENT OF UGANDA

shots.narration: Amin was famous all over the world, and not for good reasons. He was loud, unpredictable, and he did not follow the rules.
shots.onScreen: Newspaper headlines about Amin spin around the portrait

shots.narration: Since he took power in 1971, tens of thousands of Ugandans had been killed under his rule.
shots.onScreen: Dark map of Uganda, a slow counter "TENS OF THOUSANDS"; no bodies shown

shots.narration: He had also broken off relations with Israel and turned openly against it.
shots.onScreen: Israeli and Ugandan flags; a torn ribbon between them

shots.narration: At about quarter past three in the morning on 28 June, Flight 139 lands at Entebbe, Uganda's main airport.
shots.onScreen: Jet lands on a dark runway, landing lights on

shots.narration: The control tower lets it land with no argument. Many later asked if Amin knew it was coming.
shots.onScreen: Tower with a lit window; chip "never proven"

shots.narration: Ugandan soldiers surround the jet. Trucks, cars and armed men on every side.
shots.onScreen: Soldiers and trucks ring the plane in floodlight

shots.narration: Entebbe has two terminals. A new one, and an old one that is hardly used any more.
shots.onScreen: Airport map: new terminal, old terminal, runways, Lake Victoria to the south

shots.narration: Remember the old terminal. Everything that happens next happens there.
shots.onScreen: Old terminal glows gold on the map
shots.motion: push in on the old terminal

shots.narration: In the old terminal, the hijackers are joined by more men already waiting in Uganda. There are now at least seven of them.
shots.onScreen: Three new silhouettes step out from the shadows; counter 4 to 7

shots.narration: The passengers walk in a line from the plane to the old terminal, between Ugandan soldiers and the hijackers.
shots.onScreen: A long line of passengers walking across the apron at dawn, guards on both sides

shots.narration: They are put in the main hall. When the hijackers rest upstairs, Ugandan soldiers guard the hostages.
shots.onScreen: Hall with mattresses on the floor, soldiers at the doors

shots.narration: Then Idi Amin arrives in person and makes a speech. He says he is only a mediator, trying to keep them safe.
shots.onScreen: Amin at the front of the hall, hostages looking up; speech bubble "I am here to help"
shots.motion: slow push from the back of the hall

shots.narration: The hijackers send their demands. Release fifty-three prisoners, forty of them held in Israel.
shots.onScreen: Demand card: "53 PRISONERS · 40 IN ISRAEL"

shots.narration: And five million dollars for the plane. The deadline is 1 July. If it passes, they say, the hostages will die.
shots.onScreen: Demand card adds "$5,000,000 · DEADLINE 1 JULY"; clock icon

shots.narration: Meanwhile, the hijackers start reading names from the passports.
shots.onScreen: A hijacker at a table with a stack of passports, reading aloud

shots.narration: Israelis and Jewish passengers are moved to a separate room. Even Jewish passengers with other passports.
shots.onScreen: Passengers led through a doorway into a second room; the doorway between them

shots.narration: For many of the older hostages, this moment brings back memories of Europe thirty years earlier.
shots.onScreen: An elderly man looks down at his sleeve; soft sepia vignette

shots.narration: One hostage, seventy-five-year-old Dora Bloch, chokes on food and is taken to a hospital in Kampala.
shots.onScreen: An elderly woman helped into a Ugandan ambulance

shots.narration: Going to hospital will cost her everything. We will come back to her.
shots.onScreen: The ambulance drives off into the dark
shots.motion: camera holds as tail lights fade

shots.narration: On 30 June and 1 July, the hijackers let more than a hundred non-Israeli hostages go. They are flown to Paris.
shots.onScreen: Groups of hostages walk to a waiting jet; counters show released numbers

shots.narration: The hijackers also offer to free the Air France crew. Captain Bacos refuses. His passengers are still here, so his crew stays too.
shots.onScreen: Bacos stands in front of his twelve crew members, arms folded

shots.narration: A hundred and six hostages are left. Ninety-four passengers, and the twelve crew.
shots.onScreen: Hall with the remaining hostages; tally card changes

shots.narration: Releasing those people in Paris looked like mercy. It turned out to be the hijackers' biggest mistake.
shots.onScreen: The plane to Paris climbs away; a red X appears on the hijackers' card

shots.narration: Meanwhile in Israel, the government has not slept.
shots.onScreen: Night in Tel Aviv, a lit government building

shots.narration: The army, the Mossad and the Shin Bet meet day and night. Generals, pilots and intelligence officers fill the room.
shots.onScreen: War room, figures around a long table with maps and phones

shots.narration: One team has one job. Find out every detail about the place where the hostages are. Every door, every window, every guard.
shots.onScreen: An analyst pins photos and drawings to a wall board

shots.narration: And then the hijackers' mistake pays off. Israeli agents fly to Paris and meet the released hostages.
shots.onScreen: Map: line from Tel Aviv to Paris

shots.narration: They ask them everything. How many hijackers? Where do the Ugandan soldiers stand? Who sleeps where? Which doors are open?
shots.onScreen: Interview room in Paris, a released hostage drawing a sketch of the hall

shots.narration: At the same time, Israel tries to talk its way out. The United States asks Egypt's president, Anwar Sadat, to put pressure on Amin.
shots.onScreen: Phones connect between Washington and Cairo

shots.narration: Even the PLO leader, Yasser Arafat, sends an envoy. The hijackers refuse to speak to him.
shots.onScreen: An envoy at the terminal door; the door stays shut
shots.motion: slow push on the shut door

shots.narration: Israel finds a retired army colonel who knows Amin personally, Baruch Bar-Lev. He calls Amin on the phone again and again.
shots.onScreen: Bar-Lev at a desk with a rotary phone; name callout
shots.overlay: callout: BARUCH BAR-LEV / RETIRED COLONEL, AMIN'S OLD FRIEND

shots.narration: He tells Amin this is his chance to be a hero. Free the hostages, he says, and you might even win the Nobel Peace Prize.
shots.onScreen: A golden medal spins in a thought bubble over the phone

shots.narration: Amin says it is out of his hands. Give them what they want, or they really will kill everyone.
shots.onScreen: Amin on the other end of the line, shrugging

shots.narration: At home, the pressure grows by the hour. The hostages' families protest outside government offices and push their way inside.
shots.onScreen: Crowd with placards outside a government building; some push through the doors

shots.narration: They are on the news every night. Bring them home, whatever it costs.
shots.onScreen: TV set showing family members; placard "BRING THEM HOME"

shots.narration: Prime Minister Yitzhak Rabin is ready to negotiate. The hostages are in an enemy country, and he will not risk their lives over prisoners.
shots.onScreen: Rabin at the head of the table; name callout

shots.narration: His defence minister, Shimon Peres, disagrees. Free terrorists today, he says, and there will be more hijackings tomorrow.
shots.onScreen: Peres stands across the table; name callout

shots.narration: They agree on one thing. Bring us a military plan, and then we will decide.
shots.onScreen: Both men look at an empty map on the table

shots.narration: On the morning of 1 July, the generals meet at army headquarters in Tel Aviv.
shots.onScreen: Kirya headquarters at dawn, cars arriving

shots.narration: Brigadier General Dan Shomron brings three plans.
shots.onScreen: Shomron at an easel with three covered boards; name callout

shots.narration: Plan one. Navy commandos cross Lake Victoria by boat and storm the terminal from the water.
shots.onScreen: Map of Lake Victoria; boat icons cross toward Entebbe

shots.narration: One problem nobody had written down. Lake Victoria is full of crocodiles.
shots.onScreen: Crocodile eyes rise out of the water next to the boat icons; red X stamps the plan

shots.narration: Plan two. Drop paratroopers onto the airport at night.
shots.onScreen: Parachute icons drift down over the map

shots.narration: Plan three. Hide commandos inside a normal passenger plane and land at Entebbe as if nothing was wrong.
shots.onScreen: Cutaway civilian jet full of commandos instead of passengers

shots.narration: All three plans get them in. None of them get them out. Every exit depends on Idi Amin helping, and nobody trusts Amin.
shots.onScreen: Three boards, each stamped with a red X

shots.narration: Shomron asks for more time to build a plan that needs nothing from Uganda.
shots.onScreen: Shomron alone at the table, maps spread out

shots.narration: So Israel buys that time. It tells the hijackers it accepts their demands, but needs a few days to gather prisoners from five countries.
shots.onScreen: Telegram slides across a table: "WE ACCEPT. NEED MORE TIME."

shots.narration: Amin likes this. He is about to fly to Mauritius to hand over the chair of the Organisation of African Unity, and a delay suits him too.
shots.onScreen: Amin boarding a plane, briefcase in hand

shots.narration: The deadline moves to 4 July. Amin goes on the radio and takes the credit.
shots.onScreen: Deadline card flips from 1 JULY to 4 JULY; Amin at a microphone

shots.narration: Then the intelligence team finds a gift. An Israeli company, Solel Boneh, built the old terminal at Entebbe in the nineteen seventies.
shots.onScreen: Blueprint unrolls on the table, "SOLEL BONEH" in the corner

shots.narration: Its engineers still have the plans. Every room, every corridor, every door.
shots.onScreen: Blueprint lines glow and extrude into a 3D terminal model
shots.motion: orbit the model as it rises

shots.narration: With the blueprints and the Paris interviews, the soldiers build a copy of the terminal and practise the raid again and again.
shots.onScreen: Night training: soldiers run through a wood and canvas mock-up

shots.narration: The final plan is bold. More than a hundred commandos fly to Uganda without asking anyone. They take the whole airport, free the hostages, and fly them home.
shots.onScreen: Animated plan on the map: planes land, teams fan out, planes leave

shots.narration: The plan only works if everything happens fast. Faster than Uganda's army can react. That is why they call it Thunderbolt.
shots.onScreen: Lightning bolt emblem flashes across the map

shots.narration: On 3 July, the cabinet approves it. By then, the planes are already in the air.
shots.onScreen: Clock on the wall; through the window, planes climbing

shots.narration: Meanwhile, at Entebbe, the hijackers are relaxed. In less than a day, they think, they will have their prisoners.
shots.onScreen: Hijackers playing cards upstairs in the terminal

shots.narration: Israel picks four C-130 Hercules transport planes for the job.
shots.onScreen: Four C-130s lined up on an Israeli airbase at sunset

shots.narration: The Hercules can land on short, rough runways and take off again fast.
shots.onScreen: A C-130 does a short landing on a dirt strip, dust cloud

shots.narration: It carries heavy loads, and its back ramp opens so cars and soldiers can roll straight out.
shots.onScreen: Cutaway C-130 showing a Mercedes, Land Rovers and soldiers inside

shots.narration: Israel to Entebbe is more than four thousand kilometres. Even full of fuel, the planes cannot make it home without refuelling.
shots.onScreen: Map: route with a fuel gauge running down to empty before Israel

shots.narration: So Israel secretly arranges to refuel in Kenya, at Nairobi, on the way back.
shots.onScreen: Map: Nairobi glows; secret handshake icon

shots.narration: They also bring a team with portable pumps, ready to steal fuel from Entebbe itself if Kenya says no.
shots.onScreen: Ten soldiers with fuel pumps and hoses

shots.narration: In the afternoon of 3 July, the four planes take off from Sharm el-Sheikh, at the tip of the Sinai.
shots.onScreen: Planes take off one by one over the sea

shots.narration: Two Boeing 707s follow. One is a flying hospital that waits in Nairobi. The other is a flying command post that circles over Entebbe.
shots.onScreen: Two 707s high above the C-130s; labels "HOSPITAL" and "COMMAND"

shots.narration: They fly down the Red Sea along the airline routes, then drop very low, just above the waves, below the radars of Egypt, Sudan and Saudi Arabia.
shots.onScreen: Map: route ribbon dips; radar circles sweep and miss the planes

shots.narration: Over Ethiopia, over Kenya, then across Lake Victoria toward Entebbe.
shots.onScreen: Map: ribbon crosses Ethiopia and Kenya to the lake

shots.narration: Each plane has its own job.
shots.onScreen: Four plane icons with numbers 1 to 4

shots.narration: Plane one carries the assault team. Twenty-nine commandos from Israel's elite unit, Sayeret Matkal, led by Yoni Netanyahu.
shots.onScreen: Cutaway of plane one, the convoy and the 29 men

shots.narration: Yoni is the older brother of a man who will one day become Israel's prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu.
shots.onScreen: Two brothers in a family photo frame

shots.narration: Plane two carries a team to take the new terminal and hold off the Ugandan army.
shots.onScreen: Plane two cutaway, soldiers with flags pointing to the new terminal

shots.narration: Plane three carries the team that will destroy Uganda's fighter jets, so nobody can chase them home.
shots.onScreen: Plane three cutaway, map arrow to the MiG line

shots.narration: Plane four is for the hostages, with doctors on board.
shots.onScreen: Plane four with stretchers and a medic

shots.narration: One minute before eleven at night, the first Hercules reaches Entebbe.
shots.onScreen: Airport map with the lead plane icon approaching from the lake

shots.narration: It comes in with its lights off, two engines shut down to keep it quiet.
shots.onScreen: Dark C-130 over the lake, two propellers still

shots.narration: The ramp opens in the air, so not one second is lost after landing.
shots.onScreen: Ramp lowering in flight, soldiers holding on inside
shots.motion: interior shot looking out the open ramp

shots.narration: On the ground, soldiers place battery lights along the runway, so the next planes can land even if Uganda turns the runway lights off.
shots.onScreen: Soldiers place small lamps along the runway edge

shots.narration: Out comes the black Mercedes and the two Land Rovers.
shots.onScreen: Ramp down, convoy rolls out

shots.narration: Amin always arrived at the airport in a black Mercedes with an escort. So the Israelis copied it. Same car, same flags, same kind of number plates.
shots.onScreen: Close detail on the flag and plate; side by side with a photo of the real convoy

shots.narration: Then they drive slowly toward the old terminal, at the speed Amin's convoy usually drove.
shots.onScreen: Convoy driving through the dark, speedometer 40 km/h

shots.narration: But they did not know one thing. A few days earlier, Amin had bought a new Mercedes. A white one.
shots.onScreen: Split frame: black Mercedes and white Mercedes; red X on the black one
shots.motion: push in on the white car

shots.narration: Three hundred metres from the terminal, two Ugandan sentries see a black Mercedes and know something is wrong. They raise their rifles.
shots.onScreen: Two sentries step into the headlights, rifles raised
shots.motion: slow push from behind the convoy

shots.narration: The commandos had orders not to fire on Ugandans. But the moment has come. A silenced shot, then a loud one from the Land Rover behind.
shots.onScreen: Cut to black on the first shot; a flash lights the dark

shots.narration: The loud shot echoes across the runway. The surprise is gone.
shots.onScreen: Wide shot of the airport, lights flicking on in windows

shots.narration: They leave the cars and run the last three hundred metres.
shots.onScreen: Silhouettes running toward the terminal

shots.narration: Soldiers on top of the old control tower open fire. Two teams stay back to fight them.
shots.onScreen: Muzzle flashes high on the tower as small star flashes; nobody shown hit

shots.narration: Yoni's team keeps running toward the main hall. Speed is everything.
shots.onScreen: Yoni at the front of the team, silhouette

shots.narration: Outside the terminal, Yoni is hit by fire from the Ugandan soldiers. He falls. The others keep going.
shots.onScreen: Yoni's silhouette stops; cut to black for one beat

shots.narration: The man who led the raid is the first to fall. The raid has barely begun.
shots.onScreen: The empty spot in the running line, lit by a single lamp

shots.narration: At the door, a hijacker steps out, and he is shot. Inside, two more hijackers turn toward the hostages, and the commandos shoot them first.
shots.onScreen: Hall doorway lit by flashes, silhouettes only

shots.narration: The commandos shout through a megaphone in Hebrew and English. Stay down. Stay down.
shots.onScreen: A commando with a megaphone; hostages flat on the mattresses

shots.narration: One young hostage stands up. In the dark, a commando takes him for a hijacker. He is killed.
shots.onScreen: A standing silhouette among the lying hostages; cut to black

shots.narration: Three hostages die in the crossfire.
shots.onScreen: Three candles on black

shots.narration: The hostages point to a side room. The last hijackers are hiding there. The commandos go in.
shots.onScreen: Door to the side room, a flash under the door

shots.narration: Every hijacker in the terminal is dead. The commandos check every room and floor.
shots.onScreen: Corridor with torch beams sweeping

shots.narration: Then the radio call goes out. We have the hostages. We are coming out.
shots.onScreen: Commando at a radio, map of the airport behind him

shots.narration: Meanwhile, the fighting is still going on outside.
shots.onScreen: Wide shot of the airport with distant flashes

shots.narration: The hostages run from the terminal to the planes, with commandos on both sides.
shots.onScreen: Line of hostages running across the apron, commandos guarding

shots.narration: A hundred and two of them are rescued.
shots.onScreen: Counter ticks to 102 as the last hostage boards

shots.narration: On the military side of the airport, the third team destroys Uganda's fighter jets in a row. Eleven MiGs. Nobody can follow them now.
shots.onScreen: Line of MiG jets; flashes roll down the row; smoke only, no people

shots.narration: In the fighting, around forty-five Ugandan soldiers are killed. Five commandos are wounded. Only one dies. Yoni.
shots.onScreen: Memorial card with numbers, no images of bodies

shots.narration: The planes were on the ground for about ninety minutes. The assault itself took around thirty.
shots.onScreen: Two clocks: 90 MIN and 30 MIN

shots.narration: They fly to Nairobi, refuel, and head north for home.
shots.onScreen: Map: Entebbe to Nairobi to Israel

shots.narration: On 4 July, they land at Ben Gurion, the same airport the hostages left from eight days earlier.
shots.onScreen: Plane lands in morning sun, crowd waiting

shots.narration: Families run onto the tarmac. People cry, sing and hug strangers.
shots.onScreen: Crowd hugging at the foot of the ramp

shots.narration: In Uganda, Amin is furious. He blames his own army and turns on Kenya, which helped the Israelis.
shots.onScreen: Amin at a desk slamming a fist; map of Kenya behind

shots.narration: Hundreds of Kenyans living in Uganda were killed in revenge.
shots.onScreen: Dark map of Uganda and Kenya

shots.narration: And Dora Bloch, the seventy-five-year-old woman taken to hospital, was never seen alive again.
shots.onScreen: Empty hospital bed, curtain drawn

shots.narration: Years later, British records and a Ugandan inquiry said she was taken from her bed and killed on Amin's orders.
shots.onScreen: Document cards: "UK GOVERNMENT FILES", "UGANDA INQUIRY 1987"
shots.overlay: chip: BRITISH FILES AND UGANDAN INQUIRY

shots.narration: In Israel, Yoni Netanyahu became a national hero. The operation was renamed in his honour. Operation Yonatan.
shots.onScreen: Memorial with a flag, title card "OPERATION YONATAN"

shots.narration: His younger brother Benjamin carried his name into politics. Twenty years later, he became prime minister.
shots.onScreen: Benjamin at a podium, generic house-style figure; date tag 1996

shots.narration: Almost fifty years on, Entebbe is still called one of the boldest rescue missions ever attempted.
shots.onScreen: The four planes fly into sunrise

shots.narration: Four planes, four thousand kilometres, in the dark, in a country that wanted them to fail.
shots.onScreen: Final wide: the old terminal at dawn, empty

shots.narration: If you want more stories like this, subscribe. See you in the next one.
shots.onScreen: End card with subscribe button
